messages.subject: MSstats (2.3.4) / Goup Comparison - inputmissingpeaks, missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
parts:
Hello,

I have a dataset of 80 raw files (Waters), into two groups ('Healthy' vs 'Disease')

Windows 7.

MSstats 2.3.4 installed without problems (MSstats_2.3.4 Rcpp_0.11.3 see sessioninfo below).

After installing MSstats (in skyline version 2.6.0.6709), running the menu item  Tools / MSstats / Group Comparison gave the following output:


================================================================
 ** Loading the required statistical software packages in R .....
 
Loading required package: Rcpp
KernSmooth 2.23 loaded
Copyright M. P. Wand 1997-2009


 =======================================
 ** Reading the data for MSstats.....


 =======================================
 ** Data Processing for analysis.....
Error in if (inputmissingpeaks == "TRUE") { :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

 Can't finish analysis.





If I look at the r script ( MSStatsGC.r ) this error seems to come from:

# missing peaks cbox
inputmissingpeaks<-arguments[12] ## last
if(inputmissingpeaks=="TRUE")

Now, I don't know where this '12' comes from but it seems quite high; after all arguments comes from the command line:

arguments<-commandArgs(trailingOnly=TRUE);


I don't know what to do further to get this to run.  The other two MSstats options ('QC', and  'Design SampleSize') run to completion without errors.
But it is exactly the 'Group Comparison' that we're most interested in.

Any advice is most welcome,

Thanks!


Erik Rijkers

Proteomics
Erasmus University Medical Center
Rotterdam
Netherlands

messages.subject: Re: MSstats (2.3.4) / Goup Comparison - inputmissingpeaks, missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
parts:
Dear Erik,

Thank you for reporting this issue and more details that you found.
In conclusion, I found that 'Group Comparision' had the bug for  group comparsion design (it was okay for time- course design). So, I updated the vew v2.3.4. Please check the post, "MSstats external tool in Skyline v2.3.4 re-updated on Oct 14". I finished several tests for multiple datasets. and everything works in my side. 

and if you are interested in more details about technically how I fixed,
'12' cames from the number of arguments that it collected from your selection in pop-up windows. high and low doesn't matter. The problem came from it could be changed. (depending on number of unique conditions) So, instead of fixed number, I calculated inside of it in order to make flexible for different designs. 

I hope that it will be helpful for you.

-- Meena
